newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki edges up with buyers absent.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki edges up with buyers absent.

text.p: Shares edged up to another all-time high close on Friday but gains were capped by an absence of buyers even as strong bonds and a low-inflation signal from the U.S. boosted sentiment, brokers said.

The FOX stock futures index rose 0.04 percent to 1,080.75, while the all-share HEX gained 0.15 percent to end at a new all-time high close of 3,143.51 points, beating the previous peak, set on Wednesday, by just over half a point.

"There were just very few buyers on the market," one broker said, adding that investors seemed to be nervously watching whether the U.S. market's upward trend would hold and that the warm summer weather had also dampened trade.
The market reacted so gingerly to a sharp downward shift in interest rates during the day that the response next week could be all the more positive, one broker said.

Trade had been kept on hold for most of the day by the U.S. May producer price index, which finally came in below forecasts and, as a low-inflation signal, set the scene for strength in the week ahead, brokers said.
Nokia ended up 0.50 markka at 364.50 in active trade, making up almost half of the 537 million markka volume.
But one broker said that with stock futures maturing next Thursday, there could be some heavier Nokia selling next week.
Food, feed and chemical group Raisio ended a volatile session flat at 420.00 markka after hitting a session high of 438.00 markka and then pitching to an intraday low of 413.00.
"It was almost a collapse," one broker said.

Brokers said the market had welcomed Raisio's announcement of a deal with French company DRT to up production of a key ingredient of its Benecol margarine. But they said some investors had apparently expected Raisio to have made even more progress on finding a foreign partner for the Benecol business.
Brokers said earnings reports from national carrier Finnair and cargo equipment and building materials group Partek sparked only mild trading interest.

Partek fell 0.50 markka to 93.50 in thin one million markka volume after reporting January-April profits up to 51 million markka, in the middle of analysts' forecasts, which had been in an unusually wide range of nil to 126 million markka.

Finnair closed 0.20 higher at 36.20, with volume rising to a modest 1.5 million markka after the group reported 12-month profits before extras and tax down 42 percent on the previous year but within the range of forecasts in a Reuters poll.
